question_text: How are PFAS samples preconcentrated before mass spectrometry, and how do protocols vary by matrix, analyte, or method?

question_components.description: Describe how PFAS samples are preconcentrated prior to mass spectrometric analysis, including the main extraction and enrichment approaches used.
Explain how preconcentration protocols differ by sample matrix (e.g., drinking water, wastewater, regeneration brine, soil/solid, slurry) and by analytical method setup.
Identify protocol variations related to analyte properties (e.g., PFOS vs PFOA vs other PFAS) or sorbent chemistry that affect preconcentration.

validated_chunk_tags.allowed_use: Use to describe a solid-phase extraction-based preconcentration protocol for PFAS in water samples prior to LC-MS/MS, including filtration, WAX SPE cartridges, preconditioning solvents, sample volume, loading rate, washing, and general elution step.

validated_chunk_tags.exact_support: Water sam- ples processed at SLU were filtrated through glass microfiber filters (47 mm diameter, Whatman TM, China). After filtration, samples were extracted through solid phase extraction (SPE) cartridges (Oasis® WAX, 6 cc, 500 mg, 60 mm; Waters, Ireland) using an established method described elsewhere ( Ahrens et al., 2010 ). Briefly, the cartridges were preconditioned with 4 mL ammonium hydroxide solution (0.1% in methanol), 4 mL methanol and 4 mL Millipore water. Before loading the water samples, 100 mL of the IS mix (20 ng mL /C0 1 for individual mass-labelled PFAS) were added to the samples in the PP bottles. 500 mL of the water samples were then loaded onto the cartridges with one drop per second. The cartridges were washed by adding 4 mL 25 mM ammonium acetate buffer in Millipore water.

validated_chunk_tags.exact_support: Water samples from the pilot test were first filtered through a 0.8 μ m membrane to remove suspended solids and then purified by solid-phase extraction (SPE) using Waters Oasis WAX cartridges (6 mL, 150 mg). The SPE cartridges were first pre-conditioned sequentially with 4 mL of 0.5 % NH 4 OH/methanol, 4 mL of methanol and 4 mL of ultrapure water. Then 20 mL of water sample was loaded at a flow rate of 2 mL/min. After that, the cartridges were washed with 4 mL of 25 mM ammonium ace - tate solution and dried with a vacuum pump. Finally, the cartridges were sequentially eluted with 4 mL of methanol and 4 mL of 0.5 % NH 4 OH/ methanol. The eluate was filtered through a 0.22 μ m membrane for PFAS analysis.

validated_chunk_tags.exact_support: Prior to quantification of PFAS concentration in samples, samples were purified using solid phase extraction (SPE) to remove high con - centration of inorganic salt. The Water Oasis Wax weak-ion-exchange SPE cartridges (3 mL, 60 mg sorbent) were first conditioned by running 5 mL of a 0.1 % (0.028 M) NH 4 OH in MeOH through them. Next, 5 mL of MeOH was used to rinse the cartridges, followed by 5 mL of Milli-Q water. Once the conditioning step was completed, 10 mL of samples were shaken vigorously and then loaded onto the cartridges. A flowrate of 2 drops per second was used for the loading process. The cartridges were then washed with 10 mL of a 25 mM sodium acetate solution. Finally, the cartridges were eluted with 5 mL of MeOH and 5 mL of 0.1 % (0.028 M) NH 4 OH in MeOH solution, respectively.

question_text: Does longer empty-bed contact time necessarily translate into better PFAS performance in granular activated carbon systems?
